To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single–item global measure of SRHR is associated with measures of ANS activity.
a single–item global measure of SRHA self–reported health is associated with measures of heart rate and heart rate variability.
a global measure self-rated health is significantly associated with HRV measures in a cross–sectional occupational sample of working adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of SRH with biomarkers of morbidity and the mechanisms linking SRH with morbidity.
the association of a global self–rated health (SRH), a single–item questionnaire measure, with markers of inflammation and other frequently used health biomarkers.
the relationship between self–rated health and a range of biomarkers, including inflammatory markers, blood glucose and lipids, as well as heart rate variability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRH is associated more strongly with HRV than with other biomarkers.
SRH is a marker for the ANS function, and that the ANS is a potential mechanism linking SRH to morbidity and mortality.
the association between SRH and biomarkers is not uniform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extent of the ANS function is more strongly associated with self-rated global health than any other biomarkers, and this association was independent of age, gender, BMI, smoking status and alcohol use.
HRV, and ANS function in general, is more closely linked to self–perception and health status than other frequently used biomarkers.
the association of self-rated health with morbidity is more strongly linked with heart rate variability than other commonly used biomarkers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ANS function may provide a more direct measure of health than commonly used markers of inflammation, lipids, and glucose.
the use of HRV in the study of health and disease is warranted.
ANS function is a strong and independent predictor of SRH, and should be considered in future work on the mechanisms of SRH.
